i18n.current: A general practitioner based in La Rochelle, I created BreathIQ out of a public-health conviction: too many patients consult too late — or too early — for lack of a clear reference point between their symptoms and global epidemic alerts. BreathIQ is my answer: free, sourced, ad-free.

i18n.reason: Dangling modifier; "consult" and "for lack of a clear reference point" are calques.

triage.current: Hard breathing. Confusion. Red or purple spots that do not fade under a glass. Stiff neck. Fits (jerking of the body). Fainting. Purple blotchy skin, or grey colour. No urine for 12 hours. Heavy bleeding. Chest pain. A child who is hard to wake. On dark skin, check inside the lips, the palms and the eye whites.
triage.proposed: Struggling to breathe. Confusion. Red or purple spots that do not fade under a glass. Stiff neck. Fits (jerking of the body). Fainting. Blotchy purple skin, or a grey colour. No urine for 12 hours. Heavy bleeding. Chest pain. A child who is hard to wake. On dark skin, check inside the lips, the palms and the eye whites.
triage.reason: "Hard breathing" is unnatural; the NHS says "struggling to breathe". Leave "Fainting" for "Malaise" as it is (deliberate, matches "syncope").

triage.proposed: Is there any of these signs? Confusion. Repeated vomiting. Dark urine. Yellow skin or eye whites. Struggling to breathe. Fainting.
triage.reason: Same "hard breathing" fix.

triage.proposed: In this baby, is there any of these signs? Struggling to breathe. Hard to wake, or not reacting. Grey or blotchy skin. Fits. Spots that do not fade under a glass. Or you cannot get quickly to the emergency department.

triage.current: Moan: a small crying sound as the air goes out.
triage.proposed: Grunting: a short noise from the throat each time the child breathes out.
triage.reason: Matches the fix above; a "crying sound" could be mistaken for normal crying.
